summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol use, was admitted after being assaulted and reporting chest pain near his defibrillator, along with episodes of hematemesis. He was initially managed in the MICU for alcohol withdrawal, receiving benzodiazepines, and was found to have elevated lactate likely due to withdrawal. His chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, with no device damage or myocardial infarction. The hematemesis was attributed to a possible Mallory-Weiss tear or gastritis, and he was treated with a proton pump inhibitor. He remained stable, tolerated a regular diet, and was restarted on anticoagulation. He expressed interest in sobriety but declined medications and discharge paperwork at discharge. He was discharged home with follow-up recommendations.
